builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted assistant is too expensive because its model uses most of the GPU memory.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's supported lower-precision weights on a copy of your serving setup.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model at its original precision, on the same GPU.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak memory, task pass rate, latency, and total serving cost at the same context and load.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: AscMLA: Unlocking FP4 Efficiency for Long-Context MLA Decoding through Asymmetric Scaling
summary: AscMLA replaces dequantization or dual-encoding workarounds for FP4 KV caches in MLA decoding by applying asymmetric K/V scaling on a single shared FP4 latent with pipelined scale delivery. It requires hardware with efficient FP4 block-scaled kernels and an MLA-based model, and adds kernel-level implementation complexity rather than a drop-in change. FP4's narrow dynamic range can degrade generation quality on outlier-heavy activations, and the claimed gains may not transfer to non-MLA architectures or unsupported GPU backends.
rationale: The method is tightly coupled to MLA architectures and vendor-specific FP4 kernel support, so it only pays off if the reader's stack already runs MLA models on compatible hardware.
technique: Asymmetric FP4 scaling for MLA KV cache

claims.statement: AscMLA replaces dequantization or dual-encoding workarounds for FP4 KV caches in MLA decoding by applying asymmetric K/V scaling on a single shared FP4 latent with pipelined scale delivery. It requires hardware with efficient FP4 block-scaled kernels and an MLA-based model, and adds kernel-level implementation complexity rather than a drop-in change. FP4's narrow dynamic range can degrade generation quality on outlier-heavy activations, and the claimed gains may not transfer to non-MLA architectures or unsupported GPU backends.
38.2% less cache memory than FP8 and geometric-mean speedups of 1.35x over TRT-LLM's FP8 and 1.26x over CAKE's NVFP4 MLA kernels.
